content.title: About
content.content: Okra (Abelmoschus esculentus) is an edible pod widely used in African, Asian, and Southern U.S. cuisines. When cooked, the pods become tender while retaining a light mucilaginous texture and a mild flavor. Okra is rich in vitamins, minerals, and dietary fiber.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Okra is sometimes called “gumbo” because of its characteristic slimy texture after cooking.
In the United States, fried okra is popular in the South, but boiled okra is commonly used in soups and stews.
Okra seeds can be pressed to produce oil that is high in linoleic acid.
The plant thrives in warm climates and can grow up to 2 meters tall.
Traditional medicine in some cultures uses okra pods to relieve constipation and aid digestion.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Cooked okra provides a good amount of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains vitamin K and folate
items.content: These nutrients are important for blood clotting and cell health, especially during pregnancy.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion, helps regulate blood sugar levels, and contributes to satiety.

items.title: Minerals: potassium, magnesium, calcium
items.content: Potassium aids fluid balance, magnesium supports muscle and nerve function, and calcium is essential for bone health.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: A 100 g serving of boiled okra contains about 30 kcal, making it a suitable choice for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to okra, such as skin rash or swelling.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Raw pods contain oxalates that can cause gastrointestinal discomfort; cooking neutralizes them.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: High potassium levels may enhance the effects of blood‑pressure‑lowering drugs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Boiled okra is used in soups, stews, vegetable casseroles, and salads. It can be added to curries, couscous, or rice dishes. For a softer texture, soak the pods in cold water before cooking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh okra pods in the refrigerator in a bag or container, where they stay crisp for up to 5 days. Cooked okra should be kept in an airtight container in the fridge and consumed within 3‑4 days.
